what_it_does: Chisel is a higher-level programming language for describing hardware circuits — think of it as Python for chip design, sitting above the low-level Verilog language most chip engineers use today. Writing correct Chisel code is still difficult, and using an AI language model to generate it automatically is an attractive idea, but this specific problem has barely been explored. ReChisel is an AI-assisted system where a large language model writes Chisel code and then checks its own output by actually compiling and simulating it — if something is wrong, the error messages feed back into the model so it can try again. An 'escape mechanism' prevents the system from getting stuck endlessly repeating the same wrong attempt, allowing it to try a fresh approach. The paper reports this reflection-and-retry loop meaningfully improves the quality of automatically generated Chisel code, though exact benchmark numbers are not confirmed from the abstract.
